summary.short: Sets the methodology for annual supervisory fees the European Commission charges providers of very large online platforms and search engines under the Digital Services Act: cost estimation, per-service basic amounts, a cap of 0.05% of worldwide profit, payment rules and reporting. Applies from the twentieth day after OJ publication.
summary.long: Adopted on 2 March 2023 under Article 43(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA), this Regulation sets how the Commission estimates and charges annual supervisory fees on providers of designated very large online platforms and very large online search engines. The overall annual costs estimated for year n+1 (human resources, operating expenditure and other items listed in Annex I) are recovered in year n through fees. Each designated service receives a basic amount proportionate to its average monthly active recipients (coefficient U, Annex II) and its days of designation (coefficient T). Each provider's fee is capped at 0.05% of its worldwide profit in the preceding financial year, and amounts above the cap are redistributed to providers below it. Providers submit financial statements by 31 August; the Commission communicates provisional amounts by 30 September, providers may submit observations within two weeks, and implementing decisions are adopted by 30 November with payment due by 31 December. Unpaid amounts are recovered with interest, without prejudice to DSA fines. The Commission reports annually on incurred costs and fees charged and publishes the report. Article 9 allows costs from 16 November 2022 to 31 December 2023 to be added to the first estimate.

notes: Only relations, entities and notes were requested; other sections are not filled. Target IDs are empty because registry IDs for the cited instruments were not supplied. The formulas in Articles 4(1), 4(3) and 4(4) and the bracket formula in Annex II are not reproduced in the text provided, so the basic-amount and residual-allocation formulas cannot be coded from it. Inconsistency: recital 7 describes the cap as 0,05 % of annual worldwide net income, while Article 5(2) uses worldwide profit in the preceding financial year. Recital 12 ends the pre-entry cost period on 1 January 2024, while Article 9(1) ends it on 31 December 2023. Entry into force is the twentieth day after OJ publication (Article 10); the publication date appears only in the header.
